new_entities.name: Oral marine collagen with vitamins
aliases: marine protein supplement for thinning hair
new_entities.description: Oral marine protein or collagen-based hair supplements often combined with micronutrients such as iron, selenium, vitamin C, or related cofactors.

new_entities.name: Hair density in thinning women
aliases: hair growth metrics in women with temporary thinning
new_entities.description: Measured terminal hair counts, shedding, or density outcomes in women reporting thinning hair or subclinical hair loss.

edges.population: adult women with self-perceived thinning hair or subclinical hair loss using marine protein or collagen-based multi-ingredient supplements
edges.mechanism: Marine protein or collagen-based supplements are proposed to supply amino acids and micronutrient cofactors that support hair-fiber synthesis, but the effect is difficult to separate from concurrent vitamins, minerals, and regression to the mean in self-perceived thinning.
edges.summary: Marine collagen-style hair supplements have some positive trial signals in women with thinning hair, especially for shedding and hair counts, but the literature is product-specific and heavily confounded by bundled vitamins and minerals. The fairest classification is mixed rather than strongly pro-growth.
edges.caveats: Most evidence comes from branded multi-ingredient supplements rather than marine collagen alone. That means any benefit cannot be attributed cleanly to collagen itself, and independent replication is limited.

evidence.citation: AblonG et al 2015 Dermatol Res Pract
evidence.notes: A 3-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating the ability of an extra-strength marine protein supplement to promote hair growth and decrease shedding in women with self-perceived thinning hair.
